critical_code_review_comments: The iter24 fix is minimal and structurally sound: (a) instance_id: Optional[str] = None on EngineerKeyGrantRegistration turns a previously-unlisted extra field into an explicit-optional, preserving the extra='forbid' wire-shape pin; (b) _drop_sidecars() is the right pattern for tolerating adjacent-surface annotations (state, endpoint_scope, scope_summary, grantor_email) on the SAME doc without weakening validation on the core schema; (c) delegating /grant + /revoke in routers/team.py to services.auth.engineer_key_grant_service.register_grant + revoke_grant establishes the single-source seam Owner Message 608 required, so both surfaces now read/write through one machinery.

list_grants_for_grantee's ValidationError→skip fallback is defensible for legacy-doc tolerance but should log the skipped grant_id + reason so silent drift on old docs remains visible. Currently the risk is small (all seeded docs are now schema-conformant) but worth a log line for future forensics.

The engineer/key_grants surface returns grants for the CALLER's own email by default (self-service inspection); passing ?grantee_email= gates the read to admin/engineer authority. This is coherent, but the semantic is worth documenting in the endpoint docstring for future callers.

Team seeder now writes engineer-schema-compatible docs (key_class + path + floor + scope + justification + lawful_basis_ref + issued_at all present). Good — this closes the schema drift that caused the iter23 500.
